title: Two diameters cross at a right angle: what shape do their ends make?
description: Two diameters of a circle cross at right angles, and the video joins their four ends. It treats the diameters as the diagonals of the new figure and uses the radii to see that they cut each other in half.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal diagonals that cut each other in half and cross at ninety degrees make a square. Watch for students who stop at a rectangle and forget the right angle between the diameters.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 3)
video_script.why: The child sees the two perpendicular diameters as diagonals that are equal, cut each other in half and cross at ninety degrees, and names the figure by that pattern.
video_script.substitution: Treat the diameters as the diagonals, use the radii to show that they bisect each other, and use the right angle to name the figure.
video_script.anchor: a circle with centre O and two perpendicular diameters PL and AM, with the four ends joined to make APML
video_script.payoff_line: Eigh P M L is a square

final_answer.spoken: eigh P M L is a square

maths_rules: AM and PL are the diagonals of APML
both are diameters of one circle, so AM = PL
OA = OM = OP = OL (radii), so each diagonal is bisected by the other at O
the diameters are perpendicular, so the diagonals meet at 90 degrees
equal diagonals that bisect each other at 90 degrees make a square
check: the four triangles at O have two radii and a right angle, so by SAS they match and all four sides are equal
video_script.design: One idea: the diagonals of the figure are the diameters, equal and bisecting each other at right angles. The circle with the two diameters stays on the board.
